messages:
amelia: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change landed (optimize-small-seqs) we see a consistent ~20-40% CPU regression on the short-prompt serving benchmark. Happening on the CPU side; GPU profiles look unchanged. I ran a quick perf sample and the flame shows hot paths in tokenization + scheduler wakeups which didn't used to show up. attaching notes below.

amelia: Quick snippet of what I ran:
```bash
# on repro box (dedicated repro with 8 synthetic short requests)
sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pgrep -f redwood-runtime) -- sleep 60
sudo perf script > perf.out
./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl perf.out > perf.folded
./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl perf.folded > perf.svg
```

amelia: flame summary (manual cursory):
- tokenizer::split_tokens ~ 18%
- scheduler::notify_one / futex wake ~ 15%
- kvcache::get_entry mutex_lock ~ 12%
- py::eval_dispatch (call overhead) ~ 10%
- kernel_selector::choose_small_kernel (fallback) ~ 8%

ryan: :eyes: thanks for the repro steps. can you drop the perf.out somewhere? also curious if the change made the selector prefer a slower small-kernel path more often — that would explain higher CPU in user-space tokenization.

amelia: uploaded perf.out & perf.svg to http://internal.redwood/perf/2065007890 (private). Quick grep from perf.script shows many stacks ending in `choose_small_kernel+0x1b` followed by Python wrapper frames.

mike: two quick asks: 1) can you run the same with `perf record -a` to catch kernel threads doing wakes? 2) also run with `-D 1` logging in the kernel selector to get per-request branch decisions. we might be mis-classifying seq-length due to rounding.

amelia: good call. re-ran with `perf record -a -F 99 -g -- sleep 60` and results bump futex/kernel-wake to the top of the stacks: lots of `futex_wait` -> `scheduler::park` sequences. attaching the top lines from `perf report --stdio`:

```
# perf report snippet
+ 30.1%  redwood-runtime  [.] scheduler::notify_one
+ 18.7%  redwood-runtime  [.] tokenizer::split_tokens
+ 12.4%  redwood-runtime  [.] kvcache::get_entry
+ 6.5%   redwood-runtime  [.] choose_small_kernel
+ 5.0%   [kernel]          [k] futex_wait
```

sara: sounds like two interacting problems: the selector shift -> more small-kernel dispatches (higher per-request overhead), and increased contention in kvcache or scheduler paths causing more context switches. do we have traces from the runtime tracing (perfetto/nsys) that align wall-clock latency spikes with CPU spikes?

amelia: I checked perfetto traces for a failed run: the GPU lane is idle during spikes, and CPU timelines show many short-lived threads waking. nvprof/nsys show nothing abnormal on GPU. so root cause likely CPU-side.

ryan: quick hypothesis: the small-kernel variant requires extra marshalling (copy/reshape) on CPU before enqueueing kernel work, so for short sequences the overhead dominates. if we switched heuristics to prefer medium kernel for bursts the latency might come down even if GPU time slightly increases. can we test toggling the selector to force the medium kernel?

amelia: yes, I forced the selector to prefer medium in the runtime config and re-ran the benchmark — CPU dropped ~25% and overall p95 latency improved ~12%, GPU utilization +3%. so this supports the marshalling overhead hypothesis.

mike: great find. we should also profile the marshalling path to see where time is spent (memcpy vs Python loops). can you capture a `perf record -e cpu-clock -g` with `objdump -d` annotated so we can map hotspot to source?

amelia: pulling an annotated perf map now. early look shows heavy time in `pybind11 trampoline` frames around `to_contiguous` + `reshape_copy` routines.

perf-bot: automated hint — run `perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf` to get DWARF frames (requires build with debug-info). Add `-k` to include kernel stacks.

ryan: FYI I traced kvcache access patterns with a quick instrument: high collision rate on the per-thread shard causing lots of mutex hops. patch idea: move to RCU-read path for reads + per-core warming to reduce lock hits.

sara: let's not jump to big impls yet. short-term plan: 1) revert kernel-selector heuristic to previous config for serving branch (canary) 2) collect DWARF-enabled perf samples for marshalling frames 3) run kvcache microbenchmark to validate contention theory.

amelia: actioning. I opened a canary rollout PR to pin selector to medium-pref for short-requests. PR: http://internal.redwood/pr/4123 (will deploy to canary cluster in 10m). I'll also schedule a 30m pairing session with @ryan to collect DWARF perf and produce a flame with resolved Python symbols.

mike: for the kvcache microbenchmark, I can drop a small harness that simulates concurrent gets/inserts with similar QPS. i'll post results by EOD. :thumbsup:

ryan: i'll run the DWARF perf once canary is up. if symbols are messy we can upload the debug build to the repro host.

amelia: thanks team — short-term rollback + data collection. keeping this thread pinned to the incident board. :spiral_notepad:

sara: thanks, flagged for postmortem if rollout affects prod. :eyes:
